The artifact critic named no alternative and correctly notes that every item reappears in un-subtracted panels, so no residual explanation is admissible; the strong dark NW-SE band with bright N and S lobes in (f) is precisely the butterfly/dipole a circular 1-D profile leaves on this elliptical, off-centre-cored galaxy and is counted neither way. With no tangential feature at fixed radius, no counter-image and no arc-like surface-brightness structure anywhere at this resolution, the evidence points away from lensing.

The only offset structure in this field is the fat northern lobe ~1.1" from the ticked core, and every panel argues against a lens: in (a) and (e) the pair reads as a peanut with continuous light from the core out past the north tick, in (b) the lobe saturates to the same level as the core (its own compact nucleus, with a point-like knot at r~1.7", PA~358 in the deep zoom), and its major axis is radial (N-S, tangential/radial axis ratio <1) rather than tangential at fixed radius - no constant-radius ridge, no curvature about the deflector, no thinning. The 'counter-image' at r~0.95", PA 160-205 in (d) is a smooth continuation of the same common envelope with no edge, no knot and a surface brightness far below the north lobe, so it fails the one-source mirror test. The artefact critic correctly finds no spike, snowball, striping or PSF wing, but that leaves the two features standing only as real sky, not as lensed sky; the concentric ripples and the dark N/S band in (c)/(f) are the known circular-model signature and were rightly not cited by anyone. Geometry's companion_projection and morphology's merger are the same physical picture and each accounts for both located items, leaving nothing standing.

Every item the scorer located is accounted for by an upheld alternative on grounds visible in the un-subtracted panels, not on forbidden grounds. The knot at r~0.32" SSW of the ticked core (item 1) is round in (d) and appears in (e) with the same white/yellow hue and surface brightness as the saturated bar-like nucleus it abuts; there is no tangential shear, no thinning into an arc, and the mirrored position at PA~5, r~0.3" is smooth halo - a second nucleus or superposed compact object, whichever of the two critics' labels one prefers, and not a lensed image. The compact orange point 2.1" due S in (c) (item 2) is present in both (a) and (b), so it is a real source but point-like with no counterpart at PA~0, and the SE fuzz at r~2.2-2.5" (item 3) is elongated along the radius vector, the wrong orientation for shear; the three lie at incompatible radii with incompatible profiles and cannot be images of one source. The deep 10" halo in (b) is smooth and boxy out to ~5" with no fixed-radius tangential feature anywhere, and panel (f) shows only the ESE-opening dark bowtie plus a bright residual core - the classic four-lobed/dipole signature of a circular profile removed from an elongated, off-centre galaxy - which is evidence neither way. Nothing survives, so D; no reviewer or deeper data is needed to settle this.

The catalogued galaxy at the ticks is a strongly E-W elongated, inclined disc (axis ratio ~0.45 in panels d and e), and every offset feature the scorer listed sits on its western side. Tracing the knots in the deep 10" panel (b) and the subtracted panel (c), the chain begins at the untruncated western envelope (PA~272, r~2.2"), passes through a second knot near PA~287 at r~2.3-2.9", and terminates on a bright, resolved, halo-bearing neighbour at r~3.2-3.3", PA~310: the radius increases monotonically with angle, which is the signature of a tidal bridge/plume onto an interacting companion, not of a tangential image at fixed radius. The whole eastern half of the field, including the PA~90-200 sector where counter-images of these features would fall, is blank at the same depth in (a), (b) and (c). The ticked object is a highly inclined disc/S0 with major axis PA~318/138, and the dominant feature in panel (f) - the bright four-lobed bowtie with a negative wedge along PA~45/225 - is exactly the artefact the azimuthally-averaged circular subtraction is stated to produce on such an elongated galaxy, so it carries no weight either way. The only real located features are two compact, round blue knots in the un-subtracted zooms (d)/(e) at r~1.3", PA~50 and r~1.4", PA~165, and a straight blue streak at r~4.6", PA~125 in (b)/(c). The SE streak's long axis points radially at the deflector and exits the frame, which is an edge-on field galaxy, not an arc; the artefact critic further showed it cannot be a diffraction spike of the bright SW star (star-to-streak direction PA~85 versus streak axis ~130/310). The ticked galaxy is a bright, smooth, saturated-cored early type: panels (d) and (e) inside 1.75" show only a single lopsided oval envelope with no knot, no thin detached filament and no ring, and panel (f) shows exactly the documented circular-profile artefact set (central dipole, N-pointing plume, concentric ripples), which is inadmissible as evidence either way. Of the three located items, the S/SW low-surface-brightness streak in (a)/(b) increases its distance from the tick centre from ~2.9" at PA~200 to ~4.9" at PA~240 (dr/dPA ~ +0.045"/deg) - the radius-versus-angle signature of a straight filament or tidal plume, not of a tangential arc; the SE object at r~3.4", PA~123 is a compact, irregular, knotty galaxy with axis ratio ~1.1-1.2 and no tangential orientation, and there is nothing at its mirror radius on the NW side; the NW/W "edge" at ~2.3" is the outermost isophote of the same envelope, joined continuously to the core with no gap. Both the geometry critic's companion_projection (items 1,2) and the morphology critic's merger/lopsided-host reading (items 1,2,3) are borne out by the pixels; the artefact critic correctly declined, since the 1/f striping in (b) runs vertically and all three items appear in un-subtracted panels. With every item accounted for by non-lens explanations and no counter-image or constant-radius tangential structure anywhere, this is a D; no deeper data is needed to settle it.

The artifact critic offered no alternative and the located features are genuinely on the sky - the compact knot ~1.1" NNW, the westward wisp and the core-to-knot ridge all appear at identical pixel positions in the un-subtracted panels (a), (b), (d), (e), so the circular-profile bowtie in (c)/(f) is not their origin and plays no part in this ruling. Item 2's plume grows monotonically in radius from ~0.9" at PA~355 to ~1.4" at PA~295, the signature of a tidal wrap, not a constant-radius tangential arc, and the knot itself is round with no measurable tangential elongation. The geometry critic independently confirms the decisive negative test: the annulus at r~1.0-1.6", PA 140-220 in (d) and (e) is smooth envelope only, with no counter-arc above the local envelope at a flux ratio limit >5:1. With no tangential curvature, no counter-image and a stellar bridge linking every northern feature to the ticked core, nothing survives; this is an interacting/merging pair, not a lens.

Every located item is accounted for by an upheld alternative on direct-panel evidence, so nothing survives. Item 2, the compact blob ~1.2-1.5" S at PA~180 with its own halo, sits at an incompatible radius and has no northern counter-arc, so it cannot be a second image of the same source; geometry's companion_projection covers items 1-2 and morphology's merger subsumes them plus item 3. Item 3, the broad NW feature, is a ~60°-wide fan whose radius grows with position angle (~0.8" at PA~300 to ~1.4" at PA~335) and whose outer edge is soft - a tidal plume opening outward, the opposite of a thin band at constant radius. The ticked object is a large, well-resolved inclined disc galaxy: panel (d) shows a smooth elliptical bulge with e~0.4 along PA~135/315 whose light is traceable past 1.7", and panel (b) shows faint outer arms and a dark inter-arm/dust wedge to the N-NW. The only located evidence is a single compact lump 0.4" SE of the ticked nucleus (obvious in the 3.5" deep panel (d) and the colour zoom (e), and confirmed present in the 10" panels (a)/(b)/(c), so the artifact critic correctly found no instrument-side explanation and offered none). But two independent critics converge on the same non-lens reading and the pixels support it: the lump is round to radially elongated, its long axis points back at the core along PA~150 rather than across it, it shows no measurable azimuthal extent (<15 deg of arc), the surface brightness between it and the primary nucleus never drops to the surrounding halo level, and the opposing side at r~0.3-0.55", PA~300-350 in both (d) and (e) is featureless at a level far below where the SE lump is obvious - no counter-image. In colour (e) the lump carries the same warm hue as the deflector core inside one common envelope, consistent with a second stellar nucleus or a superposed companion in a minor merger. The bright off-centre blob and the concentric ripples/bowtie fringing in (f) are precisely what the stated circular-profile subtraction produces on an off-centre, blended, elliptical core and carry no weight either way. With both alternatives upheld over both items, nothing survives; the NW disc galaxy at ~3.2-3.5" is an unrelated projection with no red envelope or group signature. Galaxy-scale field, no lensing evidence.

Nothing survives. The two offset objects the scorer flagged (item 1 at r≈1.35", PA≈290; item 2 at r≈1.12", PA≈206) are unambiguously resolved in the 3.5" deep panel (d) as small galaxies with bright, centrally peaked nuclei wrapped in round/elliptical halos — the SSW one is the second-brightest core in the field — and their isophotal major axes run radially or obliquely, never tangentially about the ticked deflector; at JWST sampling an arc would have to show tangential curvature and an extended low-contrast ridge, and neither does. Their position angles differ by only ~84°, radii by ~20%, and the 10" deep panel (b) shows no counter-image at the complementary angles, so the geometry critic's companion_projection reading is upheld for both. The morphology critic's merger reading is upheld across all three items: panels (b) and (c) show a single diffuse envelope enclosing the trio with no outer edge, which also explains the NE 'extension' of item 3, as does the artifact critic's PSF-wing alternative pointing at the bright neighbour ~2.6" at PA≈42 — the two explanations overlap and both are non-lensing. The dark bowtie/dipole cutting across panel (f) is exactly the stated circular-model artefact on this off-centre, companion-blended core and carries no weight either way, and the thin straight streak at PA≈150 in (a)/(b) is instrumental/trail, touching none of the items. This is a compact interacting group, not a lens.

The artifact critic found no instrumental explanation and named no alternative, correctly noting that both features appear in the un-subtracted deep panels (b) and (d) and in both filters of the colour panels, so the panel-(f) butterfly/dipole caveat is irrelevant here and neither feature is a subtraction residual, cosmic ray or spike (nothing in the field raises a 6-spike pattern, and the NW needle has no counter-ray at PA~115-145). But being real sky is not being a lens: the two surviving candidates fail the geometric tests on pixels that both remaining critics measured the same way.
